title: What a budget is actually for

scenes.heading: What a budget is actually for
scenes.narration: A budget has a bad reputation. People picture tracking every coffee and feeling guilty. Here's what a budget is really for.

scenes.heading: A plan made before the month starts
scenes.narration: A budget is a plan for your money, made before the month starts. You decide where your pay goes, instead of wondering where it went. It's not about saying no. It's about saying yes on purpose.

scenes.heading: Three buckets
scenes.narration: Most budgets sort money into three buckets. Needs are the must-pays, like rent, groceries and minimum debt payments. Wants are the fun stuff. And future you is saving and paying down debt. One common starting split is 50, 30 and 20 percent.

chart.note: One common starting split, not a rule. Yours can be different.

scenes.heading: Example: $2,400 take-home pay
scenes.narration: Say you take home $2,400 a month. With that split, $1,200 goes to needs, $720 to wants, and $480 to future you. If rent is high, needs can take more for a while, and the other buckets shrink.

scenes.heading: Keep it simple
scenes.narration: Here's the part most people miss. A plan you can keep beats a perfect plan you quit in week two. Round the numbers, check in once a week, and adjust next month if you overspend.

scenes.heading: Recap
scenes.narration: Quick recap. A budget is a plan you make before the month starts. Most budgets use three buckets: needs, wants and future you. And a plan you can keep beats a perfect plan you quit.
